title: Classify Story And Vitest Config File Families In Taxonomy
description: Two file-kind-collision families violate the physicalLeafRendering "kind-only basename" statute: (A) 🧪️story.tsx — 42 files under 🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🖱️ui/🧱️elements/*/, co-located storybook stories that share a directory with the component's canonical 🟦️.tsx entry (from ticket 26/08/05/UI-ELEMENT-CO-LOCATION-RESTRUCTURE W7). (B) 🧪️vitest.config.ts — 29 files across ✏️s, 🧰️framework, 🌎️hub package roots; configurableEntryContracts["vitest-config-entry"] already declares canonical filename 🟦️.ts, configured via 📜️script.ts:runVitest's --config flag, but that collides with the package's typescript-library-entry 🟦️.ts at the same package root. Determine correct registered placement per family via semanticDirectoryKinds/semanticDirectoryMemberKinds (slugPattern + parentKindIds), execute only where the registered vocabulary admits it without inventing a new directory/file kind, repoint every reference repo-wide (script.ts runVitest call sites, storybook glob in .storybook/scopes.ts, project.json/package.json), and verify `bun 📜️script.ts verify taxonomy` still loads plus run affected vitest suites in the foreground.
summary:
Classified both families against the registered taxonomy vocabulary (semanticDirectoryKinds/semanticDirectoryMemberKinds + configurableEntryContracts).

Family A (story.tsx, 42 co-located Storybook stories under elements/*/): storyFileKindId is typescript-source, so a story's canonical name (.tsx) collides with the sibling component entry already occupying that slot in the same directory. No unrestricted (parentKindIds-free) semanticDirectoryKind fits: `tests` already holds the real unit-test file in ~15 of these dirs (would collide/misclassify), `examples` is a heavily-established, structurally different convention. Confirmed via .storybook/scopes.ts's own comment that ticket 26/08/05/UI-ELEMENT-CO-LOCATION-RESTRUCTURE already hit this exact wall and accepted the current filename as a documented, deliberate exception outside the registered vocabulary. Left all 42 files and the storybook glob untouched — full findings in research.md.

Family B (vitest.config.ts, 30 files: 29 package roots + repo root): configurableEntryContracts["vitest-config-entry"] already declares the canonical filename (role tool-metadata, configured via script.ts:runVitest --config). The `tests` directory kind (no parentKindIds restriction) is proven precedent (existing unit-test files use the same pattern everywhere) and never collided with any of the 29 package roots. Moved every file into a tests subdirectory under its owner; universally rewrapped each file's own-directory capture with one more parent-directory hop so every downstream relative include/alias/coverage path keeps pointing at the unchanged package root — verified live via 6 foreground vitest runs spanning every structural category (root always resolved correctly). Repointed every real reference repo-wide: the shared helper's default parameter, ~30 explicit call sites, VS Code's config search pattern, the package-scaffold generator's default, a self-test's expected literals, one generatorContracts entry, and two basename-equality gates rewritten to check directory+basename since the filename alone is no longer unique. Left untouched: two explicitly frozen byte-pinned fixtures plus three sibling fixtures encoding the same historical wgpu-renderer/jcoprobe-guest migration replay scenario (synthetic fixture-driven test data, not live filesystem reads), and the layering ratchet (its regen command is currently blocked by an unrelated pre-existing missing-build-artifact error in a different generatorContracts entry). Two unrelated pre-existing test failures were encountered during verification (a generator launcher-count drift and a concurrent in-flight component-entry rename) and confirmed unrelated by direct root-cause inspection. Full verification transcript in verification.md. Flagged a related but out-of-scope finding (duplicate 🧪️fixtures vs 🧫️fixtures directories) via spawn_task rather than acting on it.
